sentences.text: Heard Sri Anshul Kumar Singhal, learned counsel for the applicants.
None appears for the opposite party No.2 even though the case has been called on in the revised call.
Names of Sri Diwakar Tiwari and Sri Shyam Kumar Verma are printed from the side of opposite party No.2 in the cause list.

2. Sri Anshul Kumar Singhal points out that vide order dated 07.02.2024, a last opportunity was given to the opposite parties to file counter affidavit, which has not been filed till date nor has anyone appeared to press this case on behalf of the opposite party No.2.

In these circumstances, he submits that the matter itself be heard and decided on merits as the pendency of the proceedings tantamount to an abuse of process of law and is an unnecessary harassment to the applicants.
3. Learned A.G.A. also states that since the matter is a complaint case, he does not propose to file a counter affidavit.

4. In view of this statement, the Court proceeds to hear the learned counsel for the applicants on merits and decide the case without any further opportunity to the opposite party No.2 to file any rebuttal to the assertions made on affidavit.

5. The challenge in the proceedings is to summoning order dated 27.01.2016 passed by Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No.3, Aligarh as well as the proceedings of Case No.158 of 2015 (Smt. Shikha Gautam vs. Manish Gautam and others) under Section 406 IPC, Police Station Gandhi Park, District Aligarh, pending in the Court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No.3,
Aligarh.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicants submits that the applicant No.1 was the husband of the opposite party No.2.
Due to matrimonial discord, fake proceedings were instituted against the applicants when the opposite party No.2 left the matrimonial home in 2008.

He further submits that an original suit for divorce was filed, which was dismissed, against which an appeal was filed,
which was also dismissed, against which a second appeal was filed before this Court and this Court,
by means of its order dated 30.03.2016 passed in Second Appeal No.908 of 2014, was pleased to allow the second appeal and set aside the judgments passed by the concerned Courts and granted a decree of divorce to the applicant.
7.

The order of this Court, granting decree of divorce to the appellant therein, was subjected to challenge before the Hon'ble the Supreme Court in Special Leave to Appeal (Civil) No.15466 of 2016,
which was dismissed vide order dated 11.03.2019 with certain directions with respect to payment of maintenance.

sentences.text: He further submits that the proceedings have attained finality and the order, passed in appeal, has not been subjected to any further revision before this Court.
He also states that the opposite party No.2 had left the matrimonial house in 2008.
Proceedings before various Courts had been continuing since 2008 and this complaint, quite belatedly, has been instituted with malicious intent in the year 2015.

He further argues that he had given a schedule of articles returned, which were Stridhan of the opposite party No.2 and the opposite party No.2, in her written statement to the plaint, where the schedule had been annexed in divorce proceedings, had admitted to receiving the said Stridhan.

He states that by concocting false allegations and giving a fictitious list in para 2 of the complaint, without there being any corresponding list in consonance with the Dowry Prohibition (Maintenance of Lists of Presents to the Bride and Bridegroom) Rules,
1985, the complaint has been filed which is an abuse of the process of law and such vexatious proceedings may be quashed.

sentences.text: 10. As has been noticed above, despite time being granted, no one has appeared for the opposite party No.2 nor has any counter affidavit been filed till date.

Despite repeated opportunities, the conduct of the opposite party No.2 of not filing a counter affidavit as also the learned counsels not appearing on behalf of opposite party No.2 indicates that the opposite party No.2 has nothing to say with respect to the assertions made on affidavit.
11. Learned A.G.A. also could not dispute the submissions made by the applicants.
However, he contends that from the perusal of the statements under Sections 200 and 202 Cr.P.C., an offence under Section 406 IPC is made out.
He further submits that there is no illegality in the impugned order as such, the application may be dismissed.
12. I have considered the rival submissions and find that proceedings of divorce have been affirmed upto the Hon'ble Supreme Court.
In the proceedings which are confirmed upto the Hon'ble Supreme Court except the maintenance to be paid, there was no stipulation with respect to payment /return of Stridhan.

The admission to receiving ornaments, as made in the written statement, specifically para No.5 of the written statement filed in response to the suit under Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act, also indicates that no Stridhan was left to be returned.

However, this Court is not embarking upon a finding of fact as to whether any Stridhan was left to be returned or not, but, it is apparent that no list of presents, as mandated under the Dowry Prohibition (Maintenance of Lists of Presents to the Bride and Bridegroom) Rules, 1985 for presents to bride and bridegroom, were prepared.

13. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of State of Harayana & Others vs. Bhajan Lal & Others 1992 SCC (Cri) 426, in para 102 of the judgment, has laid down the following parameters for quashing of FIR/Complaint/ Proceedings :
"102.

entities.text: State of Harayana & Others vs. Bhajan Lal & Others 1992 SCC (Cri) 426
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the backdrop of the interpretation of the various relevant provisions of the Code under Chapter XIV and of the principles of law enunciated by this Court in a series of decisions relating to the exercise of the extraordinary power under Article 226 or the inherent powers under Section 482 of the Code which we have extracted and reproduced above, we have given the following categories of cases by way of illustration wherein such power could be exercised either to prevent abuse of the process of any court or otherwise to secure the ends of justice, though it may not be possible to lay down any precise, clearly defined and sufficiently channelised and inflexible guidelines or rigid formulae and to give an exhaustive list of myriad kinds of cases wherein such power should be exercised.

(1) Where the allegations made in the first information report or the complaint, even if they are taken at their face value and accepted in their entirety do not prima facie constitute any offence or make out a case against the accused.

(2) Where the allegations in the first information report and other materials, if any,
accompanying the FIR do not disclose a cognizable offence, justifying an investigation by police officers under Section 156(1) of the Code except under an order of a Magistrate within the purview of Section 155(2) of the Code.

(3) Where the uncontroverted allegations made in the FIR or complaint and the evidence collected in support of the same do not disclose the commission of any offence and make out a case against the accused.

(4) Where, the allegations in the FIR do not constitute a cognizable offence but constitute only a non-cognizable offence, no investigation is permitted by a police officer without an order of a Magistrate as contemplated under Section 155(2) of the Code.

(5) Where the allegations made in the FIR or complaint are so absurd and inherently improbable on the basis of which no prudent person can ever reach a just conclusion that there is sufficient ground for proceeding against the accused.

(6) Where there is an express legal bar engrafted in any of the provisions of the Code or the concerned Act (under which a criminal proceeding is instituted) to the institution and continuance of the proceedings and/or where there is a specific provision in the Code or the concerned Act, providing efficacious redress for the grievance of the aggrieved party.

Manish Gautam And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 4 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24731957/
4 (7) Where a criminal proceeding is manifestly attended with mala fide and/or where the proceeding is maliciously instituted with an ulterior motive for wreaking vengeance on the accused and with a view to spite him due to private and personal grudge."

entities.text: Manish Gautam And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 14. From the discussions, made above, the case of the applicants is squarely covered in Para 102 sub clause (7) of the above mentioned judgment of Hon'ble the Supreme Court.
and this Court finds that the proceedings have been instituted maliciously and deserve to be quashed.
15. In the result, the application stands allowed.

16. The summoning order dated 27.01.2016 passed by Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No.3, Aligarh as well as entire proceedings of Case No.158 of 2015 (Smt. Shikha Gautam vs. Manish Gautam and others) under Section 406 IPC, Police Station Gandhi Park, District Aligarh, pending in the Court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No.3, Aligarh, are hereby quashed.
